Summary of every decision:

**`ZeroValueProvider<T>`** — a named `@FunctionalInterface` rather than reusing `Supplier<T>`. The distinct name makes the intent clear at call sites (`() -> 0` vs a generic supplier).

**`RangeSumQuery<T>`** — `int[] toArray()` replaced with `List<T> toList()`, avoiding the generic-array problem (`new T[n]` is illegal in Java). `T rangeSum(int l, int r)` is kept; range queries are still O(1).

**`PrefixCalculator<T>`** — the SAM becomes `List<T> calculate(List<T>, BinaryOperator<T>, ZeroValueProvider<T>)`. All three strategies updated: `iterative()` and `recursive()` thread the operator and zero through normally; `parallel()` uses `Arrays.parallelPrefix(T[], BinaryOperator<T>)` (which has a generic overload in the JDK) and needs only a single `@SuppressWarnings` for the `Object[]`→`T[]` cast that erasure makes safe at runtime.

**`PrefixSum<T>`** — gains a `difference` operator (`BinaryOperator<T>`) because `rangeSum` for a generic type can't assume subtraction exists. `prefix[r] - prefix[l-1]` becomes `difference.apply(prefix.get(r), prefix.get(l-1))`. The `of(int[])` convenience overload is kept and wires up `Integer::sum`, `() -> 0`, and `(a, b) -> a - b` automatically so existing call sites are unaffected.

Summary of every decision:

**`ZeroValueProvider<T>`** — a named `@FunctionalInterface` rather than reusing `Supplier<T>`. The distinct name makes the intent clear at call sites (`() -> 0` vs a generic supplier).

**`RangeSumQuery<T>`** — `int[] toArray()` replaced with `List<T> toList()`, avoiding the generic-array problem (`new T[n]` is illegal in Java). `T rangeSum(int l, int r)` is kept; range queries are still O(1).

**`PrefixCalculator<T>`** — the SAM becomes `List<T> calculate(List<T>, BinaryOperator<T>, ZeroValueProvider<T>)`. All three strategies updated: `iterative()` and `recursive()` thread the operator and zero through normally; `parallel()` uses `Arrays.parallelPrefix(T[], BinaryOperator<T>)` (which has a generic overload in the JDK) and needs only a single `@SuppressWarnings` for the `Object[]`→`T[]` cast that erasure makes safe at runtime.

**`PrefixSum<T>`** — gains a `difference` operator (`BinaryOperator<T>`) because `rangeSum` for a generic type can't assume subtraction exists. `prefix[r] - prefix[l-1]` becomes `difference.apply(prefix.get(r), prefix.get(l-1))`. The `of(int[])` convenience overload is kept and wires up `Integer::sum`, `() -> 0`, and `(a, b) -> a - b` automatically so existing call sites are unaffected.
